items.quote: In quarter one, we will more than double our presence adding one store for EV auto, every two days.

items.statement: Triumph domestic network to scale to 150 stores in H1 FY25
items.quote: scale up the domestic network to 150 stores within the first half

items.statement: Exports revenue ~$460 million in Q4 FY24, grew double-digit with better realization and richer mix
items.quote: The approximate $460 million of revenue that we've had on exports, therefore, gre w double digit and further benefit from better realization and a richer mix, notably more sports and premium motorcycles and commercial vehicles.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA INR2,307 crores, 34% YoY growth, enterprise margin steady at 20%
items.quote: EBITDA came in at INR2,307 crores, a very strong growth of 34% year -on-year with the ent erprise margin holding steady at the 20% level.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 19.7%, up 180 bps YoY, added ~400 bps over 2 years while scaling EV business
items.quote: EBITDA at nearly INR9,000 crores was up 35% year-on-year on the back of very solid margin expansion of 180 basis points. At a full year margin of 19.7%, we have now added almost 400 basis points of margin in the last 2 years.

items.statement: EV 2-wheeler unit profitability still distance away even with PLI; cost rationalization bridging gap
items.quote: Will PLI in the case of the electric 2-wheeler lead to a unit-level profitability, the answer to that is no. Still some distance away. I think between a mix, it certainly helps address a large part of the drag. But I think with work that is happening on cost rationalization, and alternate sourcing, we're clearly bridging that gap.

items.statement: EV 3-wheeler with PLI now as profitable as ICE 3-wheelers
items.quote: On the electric 3-wheeler, I think we've said this and to reinforce with the PLI, we are definitely as profitable as the ICE 3-wheelers.

items.statement: Commodity basket neutral in Q4; zinc and ABS tight, noble metals soft; aluminium and copper seeing slight step-up recently
items.quote: On commodities, the overall basket, let's say is by and large neutral - steel, aluminium, lead, and rubber were about flattish. Zinc and ABS saw some tightness, whereas the noble metals portfolio across all 3 rhodium, platinum & palladium and nickel were relatively soft.

items.statement: Domestic motorcycle retail grew 4x industry in 125cc+ segment; 75% of business from 125cc+ vs industry 52%
items.quote: In quarter 4, our retails grew at twice the rate of others, and in the 125cc plus segment, our retail grew 4x than others. 75% of our business comes from the 125cc plus segment, while for the industry, the ratio is 52%.

items.statement: Pulsar brand became INR10,000 crores brand; 6 new models launching in H1 FY25 starting with biggest Pulsar in May
items.quote: Pulsar has now become a INR10,000 crores brand. Further 6 models will be launched in H1 of FY '25, beginning with the biggest Pulsar in early May, ensuring that we set a relentless pace and are always top of mind of th e customer.

items.statement: World's first CNG bike launching to target mileage-conscious commuter segment >600,000 units/month
items.quote: We will also take aim at the mileage conscious commuter by launching the world's first CNG bike, which will half the commuting expenses of the common man.

items.statement: Chetak EV Q4 sales ~40,000 units, market share rose from 5% to 13% YoY; more than all of FY23
items.quote: Chetak delivered its highest quarterly numbers of nearly 40,000 units with significant share gain, moved from 5% same time last year to 13% as it currently stands during this time. And to put this in perspective, this time's quarterly number of about 40,000 Chetak's was more than the electric scooters that we sold in all of financial year '23.

items.statement: Free cash flow INR6,600 crores in FY24, up 40% YoY, all-time high
items.quote: The emphasis on cash generation and high cash conversion, which is essentially profit to net cash, saw INR6,600 crores of free cash flow being added during the year. This was again at an all-time high and up 40% over the previous year.

items.statement: Year-end net surplus funds over INR16,000 crores after INR9,000 crores shareholder payouts in FY24
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to remain very strong with the year -end net surplus funds at over INR16,000 crores and this is even after a sizable payout to shareholders, which between the dividend in July and the recently concluded buyback was of an order of nearly INR9,000 crores.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend INR80/share; FY24 total payout ~INR7,200 crores (>95% of PAT)
items.quote: Finally, the Board earlier today recommended a final dividend of INR80 per share. This, along with the share buyback that we just concluded last month, will add up to almost INR7,200-odd crores of cash that we are paying out to shareholders relating t o FY '24, which translates to an industry-leading payout of over 95% of our profit after tax.

items.statement: Received PLI certificates for all 5 electric 3-wheeler models and both Chetak models
items.quote: On PLI, we are happy to report back that we have now received the PLI certificates for all five of our electric 3-wheeler models and very recently for both our Chetaks, right? So, we have the PLI certification from the testing agency in the bag as we speak and therefore, eligible going forward.

items.statement: Egypt formally recognized quadricycle category for public transport; first Qute exports within April 2024
items.quote: We are also delighted that the Egyptian government has formally recognized the category of quadricycles for public transportation, and we will commence the first exports of Qute to Egypt within this month.

items.statement: Domestic 2W financing penetration 75%, 3W financing penetration 90% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Raghu, your question on what the financing penetration in motorcycles was, that's about 75% comparable to last quarter. And in 3-wheelers, it is about 90%.

items.statement: Goal to maintain top quartile growth while maintaining margins at current year levels over next 12 months
items.quote: During the next 12 months, given the challenging macro environment, our goal is to maintain top quartile growth , while maintaining margins at the current year.

items.statement: Medium-term target to improve margins by 200 to 300 basis points over next 3 years
items.quote: We will be working towards improving utilization, onsite - offshore mix, and other operational efficiencies to ensure we keep moving towards our medium-term target of improving margins by 200 to 300 basis points over the next 3 years.

items.statement: Q4 EBIT margin at 14.45%, flat sequentially due to ramp-up costs offset by earnout reduction
items.quote: Our EBIT margin for Q4 came in at 14.45%. The Q4 EBIT margin was in a narrow band compared to the last quarter.

items.statement: Full year FY24 EBIT margin 14.4% vs 14.9% in FY23, decline due to sales, marketing and AI investments
items.quote: EBIT for the full fiscal year 2024 was 14.4% compared to 14.9% in FY23. And you will notice , that majority of EBIT decline is attributable to the investment we have made in building sales and marketing capacity, as well as building next -gen technology assets, including in the AI domain.

items.statement: Recurring EBIT margin estimated at 14.5% excluding one-time earnout reversal and transition costs
items.quote: I think we have a good Persistent Systems Limited line of sight to have EBIT margins in the normal operations at the level of 14

items.statement: Q4 TCV $447.7M with new bookings $302M; ACV $316.8M with new bookings $184.5M
items.quote: The total contract value for the quarter came in at $447.7 million, with TCV of new bookings being $302 million. The annual contract component of this TCV is $316.8 million, of which ACV from new bookings contributed $184.5 million.

items.statement: Healthcare Life Sciences to lead growth in FY25 followed by BFSI and Tech; BFSI seeing new large account ramp-ups
items.quote: the pecking order for us for this financial year would be basically Healthcare Life Sciences followed by BFSI and Tech companies. BFSI and Tech companies will kind of, depending on the different quarters, be neck to neck or a little ahead of each other.

items.statement: No improvement in demand environment seen; preparing for status quo demand conditions
items.quote: We are not seeing any of that. We are seeing the same kind of demand environment that was there 2 quarters or 3 quarters back and we will be happy to see a change in the demand environment.

items.statement: Top 10 customer concentration reached 40% for first time since Q1 FY23; top 5 up 7.9% QoQ, top 10 up 5.4% QoQ
items.quote: From a client concentration perspective, the contribution from top 10 customers reached 40% in this quarter for the first time since Q1 FY23.

items.statement: Top 1 customer declined $3.2M QoQ due to planned ramp-down of 5-year deal; no renegotiation or contract changes
items.quote: Our top one customer declined by $3.2 million quarter on quarter. This was in line with a planned partial ramp down of a large five-year deal that we had announced in FY23.

items.statement: Operational CapEx for Q4 Rs. 295.5 million; total cash and investments Rs. 18,585 million
items.quote: The Operational CapEx for the quarter was Rs. 295.5 million. Total cash and investments on the books are Rs. 18,585 million as compared to Rs 18,472 million at the end of previous quarter.

items.statement: M&A focus on Healthcare Life Sciences/BFSI and Data/AI cusp; targeting payer-provider ecosystem, Western Europe business, Eastern Europe delivery; evaluating tuck-in acquisitions
items.quote: So, we are looking at the cusp of Healthcare Life Sciences or BFSI and Data/AI. That's one part of it. Within Healthcare Life Sciences, we are predominantly looking at things like the payer -provider ecosystem or t he payvider, if we may call it. That is one part where we are focused on. Similarly, within BFSI there are certain macro segments that we are focused on. In terms of geography, interest

items.statement: SASVA AI platform used as accelerator in services bids, not licensed as product; GenAI Hub for enterprise transformation with Azure OpenAI, GPT-4, LangChain
items.quote: Our clients have definitely asked us for the licensing order for this but our attempt here is not to use this as a product, but use this as an accelerator, as an IT that we will use so that we can retain the value and capture more value in services as we go around rather than just using it as another part of our Accelerite business or payments.

items.statement: 178 customers with >$1M TTM revenue; new entries in $30M+, $10-20M, $5-10M buckets
items.quote: In Q4, we reported a total of 178 customers with trailing 12-month revenue in excess of USD 1 million. I'm happy to report the entry of new customers in the $30 million plus, $10 to $20 million, and $5 to $10 million buckets.

items.statement: Contractor cost increased to 14.1% of revenue due to onsite ramp-up; one-time transition cost impacted margins 110 bps; travel cost up 40 bps
items.quote: You will notice the contractor cost in this quarter has increased to 14.1% of revenues. There was one -time cost of transition related to this ramp -up in multiple deals , which impacted margins by 110 basis points.

items.statement: Targeting carbon neutrality for Scope 1 and 2 emissions and 100% renewable energy by mid-FY25; committed to science-based net zero with SBTi
items.quote: our aspiration is to achieve carbon neutrality for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, and 100% renewable energy sourcing by the middle of FY25, and I am happy to say we are well on the way to do the same. We are also committed to set near and long -term company-wide emission reductions in line with science-based net zero with the SPTI.

items.statement: Hi-Tech segment under pressure due to enterprise customer challenges; expecting pressure for next few quarters
items.quote: Hi-tech segment is obviously facing the headwinds because of the enterprise customers. Enterprise customers face challenges in their business. Their downstream ability to buy from these enterprise software companies which is what comprises hi -tech for us pre-dominantly is under pressure. So we do expect that for the next few quarters, there will be pressure in this segment.

items.statement: Added lateral hires offshore to build capacity for future growth; freshers from Q2 now in billable pool reducing utilization temporarily
items.quote: During this quarter, we also added lateral hires at offshore to build capacity for future growth, and planned transition from on-site to offshore in certain projects. This impacted utilization , and in turn margins , by about 50 basis points. Further, the freshers who had joined us in Q2 , are now part of the billable pool.

items.statement: Winning against larger IT peers in vendor consolidation deals across Healthcare, BFSI, Tech; customers unhappy with large incumbents
items.quote: More and more, we are seeing a pattern where bigger customers are not very happy with the large incumbent providers that they have. We are being invited in. We are winning against these in the larger landscape and some of the ramp ups that you're seeing in different industry verticals are based on that.

items.statement: No borrowings mentioned; free cash flow Rs. 7,325M for FY24 vs Rs. 925M prior year due to no acquisitions
items.quote: The free cash flow for the year was Rs. 7,325 million as compared to Rs. 925 million, as there were no acquisitions during the year.

items.statement: Private sector growth expected at 12-15%; HDFC Life aims to grow at least that, if not higher
items.quote: We don't really give guidance, except for saying that historically, the private sector has grown in the range of 12% to 15%. So, we should grow at least by that, if not a shade higher than that.

items.statement: VNB growth expected to track APE growth; willing to trade off margins for VNB growth
items.quote: We believe that VNB growth will continue to be led by APE growth. If we see significant incremental growth opportunities, we will be flexible to trade-off margins while maximizing VNB growth.

items.statement: Tier 2/3 markets grew 13% vs overall 1%; two-thirds of new business from non-tier 1 cities
items.quote: Two-thirds of our new business that we have written this year has come from non-tier 1 cities. Or another way of looking at it is that while overall unadjusted growth is 1%, growth from tier 2/3 is 13%.

items.statement: Retail protection grew 27% on individual APE; momentum expected to sustain
items.quote: Retail protection grew by 27% based on individual APE and we believe that the momentum will sustain into FY25.

items.statement: New business margin 26.3%, down 130 bps YoY due to operating leverage gap (70 bps) and higher ULIP mix (40 bps)
items.quote: Our new business margins are 26.3% compared to 27.6% last year. The drop of 130 bps was primarily due to 2 reasons, the first one amounting to 70 bps being the operating leverage gap caused by the one-time 1000 cr additional APE received in FY23 due to budget changes and the second one amounting to 40 bps due to higher UL proportion, thanks to buoyant equity markets.

items.statement: Protection and annuity pricing pressure has reduced inherent segment margins vs 3-4 years ago
items.quote: While the margins on protection are fairly healthy still, they are obviously lower than what they were 3 to 4 years ago. From a real -world perspective, that's something that we hav e to acknowledge as a sector

items.statement: VNB Rs 3,501 crore, down 5% YoY; 2-year CAGR 14%; EV Rs 47,468 crore; operating RoEV 17.5%
items.quote: Value of new business is Rs. 3,501 crore, implying a YoY degrowth of 5% and a 2 year CAGR of 14%. Embedded value stands at Rs 47,468 crore, with an operating return on embedded value of 17.5%.

items.statement: Sum assured grew 47%; average sum assured per policy up 33% overall, 39% for savings
items.quote: Sum assured witnessed robust growth of 47% aided by growth in pure term, ROP, higher protection cover embedded in savings products and riders  With product innovation across product s egments, our average sum assured per policy has increased by 33% on overall basis and 39% for savings business

items.statement: Number of policies up 11% (3x industry); Q4 NOP growth 14%; insured 6.6 crore lives
items.quote: In line with our intent to broaden the customer base, the number of policies for the year increased by 11%, which is almost 3x overall industry growth, based on first eleven months data. In Q4, NOP growth was 14%.

items.statement: ULIP share rose from 19% to 35% YoY; Q4 ULIP ~30%; non-par savings increased in Q4 due to Click2Achieve
items.quote: ULIPs continue to see strong traction driven by buoyant equity markets, with a surge in popularity even in higher than Rs. 2.5 lakh segment. Click2Achieve, our first DIY non-par savings solution has been received well across channels, leading to a healthy increase in the non-par savings proportion in the last quarter.

items.statement: 70%+ retail customers new to HDFC Life; nearly half below age 35
items.quote: More than 70% of the retail customers on-boarded are new to HDFC Life and almost half of these are below the age of 35 years.

items.statement: Agency channel: 80,000+ agents added; ranked #2 in distribution expansion; 75 branches opened; target 600+ touchpoints next year
items.quote: Our Agency channel is ranked No.2 in the industry in terms of distribution expansion for first eleven months, with over 80,000 agents added during the year. Moreover, we opened 75 branches in FY24 and anticipate our presence to exceed 600 touchpoints in the next fiscal year.

items.statement: Renewal collections grew 18% YoY; 13th month persistency 87%, 61st month 53%; expect shift in 13th persistency due to mix
items.quote: Renewal collections grew by 18% YoY, demonstrating our customers' continued trust in us. Persistency for the 13th month and 61st month was 87% and 53% respectively. We anticipate a shift in 13th persistency going forward, influenced by the product mix and prevalent customer segments in FY24.

items.statement: Solvency ratio 187% (regulatory minimum 150%); actual solvency capital ~Rs 15,000 crore; comfortable cushion
items.quote: 187%. In rupees crore, it's a very big number because our actual solvency in capital we have is around INR 15,000 crores. That gives us the comfort that it does not restrain growth even if ULIP mix had to go a little higher

items.statement: PAT Rs 1,569 crore, up 15% YoY; final dividend Rs 2/share (~Rs 430 crore payout)
items.quote: We have delivered a strong profit after tax of Rs. 1,569 crore, implying a YoY increase of 15%, fuelled by 18% increase in profit emergence from back book. Solvency continues to be healthy at 187%. The Board has recommended a final dividend of Rs. 2 per share, aggregating to payout of about Rs 430 crore

items.statement: HDFC Pension AUM crossed Rs 75,000 crore, up 70%; market share 43% (market leader)
items.quote: Our subsidiary, HDFC Pension Management Company, achieved a milestone by crossing the Rs 75,000 crore AUM mark, showcasing remarkable growth of 70%. We have maintained our market leadership in the pension category, commanding a market share of 43%.

items.statement: Competitive intensity high due to few listed peers; listing roadmap for private insurers seen as inevitable
items.quote: So the competitive intensity will only continue to go up until the roadmap to listing starts happening. Are there such plans? I'm sure that there used to be earlier, but that's the natural culmination. So it's a matter of when and not if that roadmap starts panning out.

items.statement: New business strain rose to 40% from 34% due to higher ULIP mix (highest strain) and operating leverage gap from low growth vs capacity
items.quote: Strain depends on the product composition and expenses. As we already mentioned on the call, operating leverage in FY24 has seen an impact of expenses which has impacted new business strain. UL has the highest strain because reserves are linked to value of the fund and since UL mix has increased significantly from 19% in FY23 to 35% in FY24 strain is higher.

items.statement: Expect sector growth of 12%-15% and aim to grow at top end or faster; targeting VNB growth similar to APE growth, implying stable margins; RoEV target 17%-18%
items.value: 12%-15% sector growth; top end or faster for company
items.quote: We are expec ting the sector to grow in this range, 12% -15%. We expect to grow at the top end of that range and hopefully faster. We are not targeting a margin expansion in this period. We are definitely continuing to see competitive intensity. We are continuing to see our distribution expansion happen, our resource allocation increasing. All of those things will, in some sense, counterbalance ea

items.statement: Holistic scorecard: industry growth 12%-15%, aim for upper end or shade more; VNB growth in similar zone; RoEV 17%-18%
items.value: 12%-15% industry growth; VNB similar zone; RoEV 17%-18%
items.quote: Holistically, we want to grow, like I said, 12% to 15% industry growth, on the upper end of that or a shade more than that would be a good place to be. VNB in similar kind of zone, return on embedded value in the 17% -18% zone, which we have again delivered. I think that kind of a holistic growth as a scorecard is what we're looking at.

items.statement: Tier 2/3 cities grew 12%-13% overall; Tier 3 grew ~17%; less than INR5 lakh cohort growing in high teens; NOP growth mid-teens
items.quote: The Tier 3 has, for instance, grown at almost 17%. Tier 2 /3 overall has grown at 13%, faster than the industry level growth . So those advantages are clearly coming in . But the less than INR5 lakhs has been growing in high teens. Our N OP growth also has been in the mid-teens in each of these segments.

items.statement: Protection growth: Tier 1 26%, Tier 2 22%, Tier 3 32%; ticket sizes only 10% differential across tiers; targeting upper quartile in Tier 2/3
items.quote: If I were to look at growth in protection, Tier 1 has grown 26%, Tier 2 has grown 22% and Tier 3 has grown 32%. And the ticket sizes are just a 10% differential between each of the tiers. If I look at each one of these different segments the growth from non -Tier 1 is healthy and the ticket size isn't that different because we are going after the upper quartile of Tier 2 and likewise for Tier 3.

items.statement: Protection margins compressed from triple digits 4-5 years ago to well above company average but far below past levels; competitive pricing pressure via aggregators; INR1 crore cover cheaper than Hong Kong
items.value: triple digits to well above company average
items.quote: Protection margins, 4-5 years back used to be in three digits. Now it is much higher than company average margins but nowhere close to where it used be.

items.statement: ULIP margins improving steadily via persistency assumption updates, product design (Smart Protect 100x cover), rider attachment, cost productivity, technology investments; margin improvement is organizational DNA
items.quote: If you were to look at steady improvement in persistency, tha t has helped because we do change our actuarial assumptions and mark -to-market it. If we see a positive trend in persistency, we wait for two years. But after two years, we do change the inherent assumptions and then new business also will get that uplift on the change in assumptions. Many such reasons that help us in go al seeking in

items.statement: VNB margin impact from operating leverage gap (capacity vs actual growth) was 130bps in FY24; not expected to repeat in FY25 as growth returns strongly; will be balanced by continued investments
items.quote: significant part of that 130 basis points is coming out of that operating leverage gap because of the difference between the capacity an d the actual growth. We do not see that repeat ing in FY 25 because we expect growth to come back fairly strongly in FY25. So that is something that will only be balanced by our continued investments.

items.statement: HDFC Bank contribution ~52%-53% of individual APE; non-HDFC Bank banca partners 12%-13% of overall business, now 20%-25% of bancassurance business (doubled over 3-4 years)
items.quote: In HDFC Bank we have gained fair market share. There has also been a little bit muted growth because of the high base in our broki ng and agenc y. We have hit almost 52%-53% kind of contribution on the individual business from HDFC Bank. It is still fairly diversified because we have many other partners.

items.statement: Credit protect business grew 13% YoY; all partners intact; market share retained despite Q4 disbursement slowdown
items.quote: The credit protect business grew by 13% for us in this year, w hich is fairly good, given in Q 4 we did see some kind of a slowdown in disbursements. All our partners remain intact in terms of our partnerships. There have been some segments where we have gone up, some segments where we have gone down , but overall we co ntinue to retain market share that we have on the credit protect business.

items.statement: Added 75 new branches last year, significant portion in Tier 2/3; 80,000 new agents added, 85%-90% from Tier 2/3; agency build-up in Tier 2/3 may take 12-18 months to deliver volumes
items.quote: Of the new agents added, the 80,000 agents added 85% to 90% of those agents are from Tier 2/3. Of the 75 branches that we have opened last year a significant portion similar kind of percentage is in Tier 2/3. All of that means that we are somewhat agnostic of channel. The channel if you visualize is the vertical and the horizontal cutting across are Tier 2 /3 opportuni ties. So it will be fairly w

items.statement: High-ticket (>INR5L) share fell from ~12% to 6%-7% of APE post-budget; non-par mix rose to mid-30s from <30% in 9M due to new product launch; ULIP mix increased in Q4 without significant margin dilution
items.quote: we had mentioned at the beginning of this year, just af ter the budget that the impact we see is that greater than INR5 lakh used to be around 12% of overall APE and today, the same category is about 6% to 7% of our business. It is definitely lower than what it was last year but it is still a fairly significant number. And that is something that we expect to continue as we go forward as well.

items.statement: Retail protection APE grew 27%; retail sum assured grew ~50%; protection share of APE inching up from 4% to 5%; expect protection to grow faster than company average
items.quote: Protection clearly for us has been growing well. And when you triangulate that with the level of sum assured, so we should, despite us not necessarily playing the price war, it should grow faster than overall company level. And we are happy that the retail sum assured has grown just shy of 50% and retail protection on a stand -alone basis has grown by 27%.

items.statement: Regulatory review report recommends product flexibility (e.g., premium holidays, lower cover multiples in GIFT City); participating in review with peers; IFRS/IndAS and risk-based capital will make sustained mispricing difficult
items.quote: Absolutely. And that is there in the regulatory review report. We are part of that , along with many other peers. I'll give you an example. Earlie r there was a caller asking about our GIFT City products. Now we have a dollar-denominated education product, which is approved by the DFSA. And there, you don't necessarily need to have a 10x cover. You could have, say, a 5x cover because your objectiv

items.statement: 13-month persistency: Tier 1 vs Tier 2 diff 300-400bps, Tier 2 vs Tier 3 similar; all tiers in 80s handle; mix effect from Tier 2/3 growth may impact headline persistency but will be priced into model
items.quote: what we have been talking about is in th e context of our expansion deeper into the Indian markets. We did speak about persistency across the 3 tiers being different by about 300 to 400 basis points at the 13 -month level, not dramatically different. All of these still put us in the 80s handle, ev en in Tier 3 market, exactly because of the ticket size at which we are operating in. We will task ou

items.statement: Assumption change impact on VNB margin: 0.2% (20bps) already baked into EV walk; persistency assumptions updated after 2-year positive trend observation
items.quote: So in VNB walk you can see a 0.2% impact on the margin due to assumption change. Some of the difference is already baked in.

items.statement: GIFT City opportunity: currently individual dollar-denominated products (education, health, travel); group term marginal (similar to DFSA); will explore credit protect if USD loans emerge from GIFT City banks
items.quote: Right now, all the products that we are looking at are in terms of individual dollar -denominated products. But tomorrow if there are banks which set up their branches out of GIFT City and they look at it, we will definitely look at similar product structures there. There are products that we will be looking at once U.S. dollar loans start coming from GIFT City.

items.statement: Economic variance ~INR1,300 crore: ~INR1,200 crore from equity, rest from lower yields vs prior year
items.value: INR1,300 crore total; INR1,200 crore equity
items.quote: On economic variance break -up. That is primarily due to equity . Out of the INR1,300 crores , INR1,200-odd crores is due to equity. The rest is due to the lower yields in this period compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Operating deleverage risk if FY25 growth falls short of 17%-18% capacity; but expect strong growth return in FY25 so gap not repeating; will balance with continued investments
items.quote: We do not see that repeat ing in FY 25 because we expect growth to come back fairly strongly in FY25. So that is something that will only be balanced by our continued investments. that's the only factor that we will talk about.

items.statement: Agency and broking channels have base effect benefit as >INR5L segment gone for the year; both channels expected to grow; banca partners (ex-HDFC) growing 13%-15%
items.quote: And third, Tier 2 /3 market in terms of products and distribution expansion , including 75 new branches that we are looking at expanding, that will also a dd. That may probably take 12 to 18 months for us to deliver in terms of agency build up in these markets and hence the business volumes coming in. But there are actually three to four lines of businesses which are helping us build the Tier 2 /3

items.statement: Competing with unlisted players with minimal disclosures; expect sector to move toward listing/disclosure roadmap which will rein in pricing exuberance in term and annuity
items.quote: I also mentioned that unlike in banks, insurance companies are largely competing with unlisted players with next-to-no disclosures. This will move and grow into a sector wherein either one lists or there is a road map or there is disclosure that are similar to listing. Something will happen. And with that, that will rein in a lot of exuberance and aggressiveness on pricing, both in term and annuit

items.statement: Channel CEOs balance top-line and bottom-line; decentralized margin management at channel level; product committee meets fortnightly to review granular product-channel-cost dynamics
items.quote: We also have channel CEOs who have to balance their top line and bottom line. If they want to sell more unit li nked, it could be through something like Smart Protect, it could be through attachment of riders , i t could be productivity improvement on costs. It could be many such things, all the technology investments that we are doing, wherein we need lesser people. It's a combination of all of t

items.statement: Industry AUM reached INR53.4 trillion with 35% YoY growth; net flows INR3.5 trillion led by actively managed equity funds at INR2.4 trillion
items.quote: The industry closed the year with AUM of INR53.4 trillion, Y-o-Y growth of 35%. Net flows for the year came in at INR3.5 trillion.

items.statement: HDFC AMC AUM surpassed INR6 trillion with 39% YoY growth and higher equity tilt
items.quote: We concluded the year with an AUM surpassing INR6 trillion, showcasing a growth of 39% year-on-year with a higher tilt towards equity-oriented assets.

items.statement: Added 3 million new customers; total unique investors 9.6 million with 16.6 million live accounts
items.quote: We witnessed healthy growth in our unique investor accoun t. We saw addition of 3 million new customers during the year, and the total number of unique investors now stand at 9.6 million with 16.6 million live

items.statement: SIP AUM represents 37% of actively managed equity-oriented AUM, in line with industry
items.quote: Notably, our SIP AUM now represents 37% of actively managed equity-oriented AUM, more or less in line with that of the industry.

items.statement: Run-rate management fees from April 1: equity ~59 bps, debt ~27-28 bps, liquid ~12-13 bps; blended ~47 bps on current AUM and mix

This is for the period starting 1st April based on the current AUM. So , assuming AUM and asset mix being constant, we shoul d be back at around 47 basis points odd from the current quarter onwards

items.statement: FY24 operating profit INR19,000 million, up 22% YoY; operating profit margin stable at 35 bps
items.quote: Operating profit for the year added up to INR19,000 million, a growth of 22% Y-o-Y with a stable operating profit margin of 35 basis points.

items.statement: Q4 operating revenue yield ~45-46 bps on quarterly average AUM; expected ~47 bps from Q1 FY25
items.quote: if you look at for the qu arter, our operating revenue reported is 6,955 And if you look at the quarterly average AUM, right, it was 6,129. So , if you look at that, based on that, it's around 45, 46 basis points is what the number is

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain ~35 bps assuming 47 bps revenue yield and 12 bps cost ratio
items.quote: Assume that 47, assume that 12, everything else being constant, then you get to 35.

items.statement: Q4 saw one-off TER compression due to year-end true-ups; direct plan TERs reinstated from April 1 (e.g., small cap 58->63 bps, hybrid debt 119->124 bps, credit risk 91->96 bps)
items.quote: there is a one-off in this quarter due to year -end true ups. We, of course, try to estimate distribution costs with utmost care and preci sion, but they are still estimates. As we see it, the same should get aligned -- starting this current quarter

items.statement: Telescopic pricing causes margin dilution as large schemes grow (Balanced Advantage TER -13 bps, Mid-cap Opportunities TER -19 bps); called 'happy dilution'

And some of our large schemes, if I look at balance advantage funds saw its AUM increase from INR520 billion to almost INR800 billion, resulting in a TER reduction of 13 basis points.

items.statement: Opened 24 new branches on Jan 2; now 254 locations (174 in B-30); will continue investing in physical and digital infrastructure
items.quote: We started the year by opening 24 new branches on 2nd of January. With that, now we are present in 254 locations, out of the 174 branches are in B-30.

items.quote: I think a large number of them are the salespeople on the ground as we have been expanding and also in some of the other capabilities that we have been building, whether it's alternatives, a lot of people in technology, in digital and client services.

items.statement: Industry SIP flows INR2 trillion in FY24 vs INR1.6 trillion FY23; March 2024 SIP flows INR193 billion
items.quote: The industry continues to set records in terms of monthly SIP flows with overall contribution for FY '24, r eaching INR2 trillion as against INR1.6 trillion in FY '23. The SIP flows in the month of March 2024 reached INR193 billion

items.statement: Flow market share in HDFC Bank channel higher than book share (book share 25-30%); engagement levels very high with dedicated resource
items.quote: happy to state that our flow market share in bank's book i s higher than the book market share. So that's encouraging

items.statement: Fintech channel growing rapidly; industry registered 17.7 million SIPs in FY24; HDFC AMC available across all fintechs with healthy share of new flows/SIPs
items.quote: In fact, as a group, they have registered 17.7 million SIPs in the current fiscal. W e are available across all fintechs and our healthy market share in new flows and new SIP

items.statement: Launched 5 sectoral/thematic funds, 5 index funds, 2 ETFs in FY24; manufacturing fund NFO opening April 26; hired 2 senior resources for private credit AIF
items.quote: During FY '24, we ex panded our product offerings in sectoral /thematic space by launching 5 new funds. On passive front, we enhanced our bouquet by laun ching 5 index funds and 2 ETFs

items.statement: Board recommended dividend INR70/share vs INR48 last year; payout ratio 77%; no stated policy but trend of increasing payout
items.quote: Board earlier today has recommended a dividend of INR70 per share as against INR48 per share last year, translating into a dividend payout ratio of 77%.

items.statement: Total expenses 12 bps of AUM in FY24 (up 12% YoY to INR680 cr); ex-ESOP up 11% to INR65 cr; 5-year cost CAGR 42%
items.quote: Our total expenses as you said, are 12 basis points for FY 24, right? This is led by people increase, investment in technology and digital.

items.statement: ESOP cost FY24 INR47 cr (non-cash); expected ~INR20 cr next year (60% first year, 30% second, 20% third)
items.quote: For the next year, I think this number is around INR20-odd crores. But it is just a noncash charge for the company.

items.statement: Competition intensity constant; distribution commission payouts unchanged; no excess brokerages paid
items.quote: I think competition intensity, I think the answer is constant. It is as good or as bad as it has been. The distribution commission payouts haven't really gone up in this quarter.

items.statement: Debt funds saw industry net outflows for 3rd consecutive year; AMFI launched 'Fixed Income Sahi Hai' campaign; HDFC AMC sees long-term potential
items.quote: This is the third consecutive year where debt fund as category has seen net outflows. So, this year was a net outflow last year as well as the year before last industry has witnessed net outflow in this category for a variety of reasons.

items.statement: Active equity market share aspiration to keep increasing from current ~13%; 17% (IPO level) not explicitly targeted but hunger remains high
items.quote: But from -- I think, given all the strength that we have, the way we have invested over the years in business, our aspiration is always to keep increasing from wherever we are.

items.statement: Margin dilution from telescopic pricing inevitable with AUM growth; management prioritizes absolute profit over statistical margin
items.quote: I'll any day take higher AUM with lower margin rather than the other way around for obvious reasons.

items.statement: Revenue guidance FY25: INR8,000-9,000 crores excluding Reliance and Nigeria (INR6,000-7,000 crores from UOV + 25-30% of INR8,000 crores new orders)

items.quote: We are looking at close to INR270 crores this year in O&M revenue.

items.quote: On the remaining IN328 crores, the intere st cost would range between INR30 crores to INR35 crores on an annualized basis unless out of free cash flows, we end up prepaying it.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance FY25: consistent with historic 10-11% range for domestic and international EPC; O&M margins at 15%
items.quote: The gross margin we said would be consistent with the gross margins which we have reported.

items.statement: No significant capex plans mentioned; business model remains asset-light and negative working capital dependent
items.quote: Business model will remain same. We are going to be asset -light and negative working capital dependent.

items.quote: Our O&M portfolio outlook continues to improve and we have seen our portfolio grow to 7.6 gigawatts as of March 24.

items.quote: We are actively pursuing projects totaling 25 gigawatts in India and 5 gigawatts in other international geographies.

items.statement: Domestic market share ~30%, PSU strike rate ~50%; Reliance discussions ongoing, expect significant portion of rollout; Nigeria MOU progressing, contract finalization expected soon

items.quote: our increased focus is on Middle East, Africa and European markets. These markets are growing strongly and we are going to focus on these particularly three markets in coming two years.

items.quote: Our net debt as of March 2024 was INR116 crores compared to nearly INR2,000 crores net debt in the previous fiscal.

items.statement: No equity fundraise planned; working capital negative, operations profitable, cash flow positive

items.statement: Trade payables increased due to March revenue spike; trade receivables + unbilled also increased; net working capital remains negative
items.quote: You will see that a lot of the revenues have happened in this quarter and especially in the month of March leading to an increase in trade payables.

items.statement: Bids based on current market prices; orders placed immediately upon receipt; protected from commodity price fluctuations
items.quote: whenever we bid, we take current prices into account. So all of our bids, when we bid out, are based on the current prices.

items.statement: ALMM not a concern; significant domestic module capacity addition; developers and PSUs have secured modules
items.quote: A significant capacity addition is happening in India. And I don't see any challenge on that particular front, with respect to EPC rollouts.

items.statement: No attrition pressure; robust leadership pipeline; hiring and developing organization for growth projections
items.quote: we have a very robust leadership pipeline, and our execution and engineering staff continues to be very, very strong.

items.quote: we are projecting around 25 crores to 30 crores, 25,000 to 30,000 crores and g rowing 15% to 25% CAGR, depending upon how the whole system, ecosystem is panning out.

items.statement: Management will not provide specific numerical guidance or outlook on metrics, focusing instead on long-term profitability trajectory
items.quote: I know you will try and ask for a lot of outlooks and guidances in various ways, during the course of this call, I'm sure. But we will be steadfast in trying to ensure that we don't give them.

items.statement: Core ROA remains in historical range after adjusting for one-off gains and provisions; aim for stability with positive bias over 2-3 years
items.quote: I think even after adjusting all these one-offs and nullifying the same, the core return on assets is in the range that we've operated in the past, and that should be a great indicator for the future as well.

items.statement: Margins expected to remain stable as cost of deposits range-bound and loan yield thresholds maintained; not chasing growth at expense of profitability
items.quote: We want to ensure that the cost of incremental deposits continues to be range bound and then whatever thresholds we have laid out a -- little bit of tweaking. We will ensure that the margins either remain stable.

items.statement: Incremental credit-deposit ratio similar to historical levels; advances mix skewed toward better-yielding retail and CRB segments
items.quote: So if you've seen for the full year, the incremental credit deposit ratio or loan deposit ratio is more or less similar to what we have always done. In fact, the advances mix is more or less towards better yielding segments li ke retail and CRB

items.quote: So willy-nilly, all things remaining same, your LDR or incremental LDR will be a tad lower for a couple of years than what we have seen in the past because we have this obligation of repaying some of the bond maturities.

items.statement: Raised lending rate thresholds across segments to offset LDR contraction; yields at respectable levels; may increase slightly further but not significantly
items.quote: Yes, yields have been one of the levers to bring down the LDR and we will use it as long as -- and we probably will use it even in future if the situation demands.

items.quote: We have not changed and it's pretty much reflected in the stability in the cost of deposits. But if there are changes because you never know the, life is very uncertain.

items.quote: We have tasked our supervisory architecture, which is 10% of the total workforce to -- in their KRAs to be measuring and monitoring all that comes in from a customer and try and see how we turn it around in the shortest possible time.

items.quote: Our asset quality continues to be very pristine. All our portfolios across segments, including early indicators, contin ue to be benign. We have, as a part of prudent risk management, created a countercyclical provision, which is a provision in good times

items.quote: At an aggregate level the overall PSL for March '24, is published or to be published, we are a little more than 52% achieved at the -- against the target of 40%. And at the same time, last year, if you see March '23, we were about 45% achievement.

items.statement: CASA ratio tepid due to high interest rate environment and structural shift in household savings; focus on gaining incremental CASA share long-term
items.quote: In a high interest rate scenario, Rahul, normally, you probably go back in time, the CASA ratios have been a little tepid. items.statement: CRB growth driven by priority sector segments (micro enterprises, small/marginal farmers, agri, weaker sections); medium/large ticket enterprises tepid due to higher threshold yields

items.statement: Merger integration complete; core metrics stable for 9 months; organization resilient; not person-dependent but process-driven with deep management bench
items.quote: We are now 9 months into the merger. The core metrics have remained stable since the time we merged with HDFC Limited. What does this demonstrate? This demonstrates that the underlying resiliency and the energy of the stand-alone franchise of the bank is very stable.

items.statement: FY24 AUM grew 22% YoY to Rs 173 billion
items.quote: In FY'24, we delivered robust growth of 22% Y-o-Y in AUM at Rs. 173 billion.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 disbursements at Rs 18.93 billion, up 39% QoQ and 20% YoY, highest ever quarterly
items.quote: In Q4 FY'24, we have delivered robust disbursement growth of 39 % Q-o-Q and 20% Y-o-Y. We disbursed Rs. 18.93 billion in Quarter 4 FY'24, taking a full year disbursement to Rs. 55.82 billion. This was our highest ever quarterly disbursement since inception.

items.statement: FY24 full year disbursements at Rs 55.82 billion
items.quote: We disbursed Rs. 18.93 billion in Quarter 4 FY'24, taking a full year disbursement to Rs. 55.82 billion.

items.statement: Opened 21 new branches in FY24 in existing states
items.quote: We have opened 21 new branches during FY'24 in our existing states to deepen our reach.

items.statement: Plans ~10% branch addition in FY25, focused on Karnataka and UP
items.quote: The branch expansion plan is around 10%, that's what we had. But as we go deeper in the South, we will look at Karnataka and other regions in those regions specifically so to say, actually. And some bit of we are already there to really look at opportunities within the existing market where we find good enough space, but specifically Karnataka, if I were to put across in this year. Rajiv, the seco

items.statement: Login to sanction TAT improved to 9 days in FY24, 8 days in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Our login to sanction turnaround time has improved to 9 days in FY'24. And for Q4FY24, we had an impressive about 8 days of TAT.

items.statement: Lead management system on Salesforce to go live in Q1 FY25, loan management system on Oracle Flexcube by first week of July
items.quote: I think from a tech transformation perspective, from the lead management we should be live by the first quarter and be active and ki cking by having successfully piloted by the time being running fully well in the quarter two, so to say. Ghanshyam Rawat: Yes, side by side LMS will be also ready. It will also go live on the first week of July

items.statement: 1+DPD at all-time low 3.12% in March 2024, GNPA at 0.94%, NNPA at 0.67%
items.quote: One day pass due has hit all time low at 3.12% in FY2024 as against 3.30% in FY2023. Gross Stage-3 stood at 0.94% and net Stage-3 stood at 0.67% as of March 31st, 2024.

items.statement: Credit cost at 11 bps in Q4 FY24 vs 21 bps in Q3 FY24, 16 bps for FY24
items.quote: Credit cost during the quarter stood at 11 basis points in Quarter 4 FY'24, versus 21 basis points in Q3 FY'24, 16 basis points in FY'24.

items.statement: BT-out rate at 0.5% per month (6% annualized) of opening AUM, let-go customers have 5x higher 1+DPD
items.quote: So, it is 0.5% every month and 6% of the opening AU M, as we speak. And in that journey, I think as an institution, we have evolved to really figure that out, what is that we need to hold. And again, a very interesting part we have also earlier declared is that the ones which we let them out have 5 times higher 1+DPDs and similar count of the GNPA

items.statement: Raised Rs 61.45 billion at 8.14% in FY24, Q4 borrowing Rs 18.52 billion at 8.14%
items.quote: In terms of borrowing, we continue d to borrow judiciously. We have raised around Rs. 61.45 billion at 8.14% during FY'24. For Q4 FY'24, we raised around Rs. 18.52 billion at 8.14 %.

items.statement: Total outstanding borrowings Rs 155.55 billion as of March 2024; mix: 47.5% bank term loans, 23.9% assignment/securitization, 19.6% NHB, 9% DCM
items.quote: Total outstanding borrowings as on 31st March 2024, stood at Rs. 155.55 billion . O verall borrowing mix as of 31st March is 47.5% from term loan from banks, 23.9% from assignment and securitization, 19.6% from National Housing Bank as refinancing, and 9% from debt capital market

items.statement: Liquidity of Rs 30.3 billion as of March 2024 including cash, unavailed CC limits and NHB sanctions
items.quote: As of 31st March 2024, we maintained a sufficient liquidity of Rs. 30.3 billion in the form of cash and cash equivalent, and unavailed CC limit and documented unavailed sanction from various banks, including Rs. 2.3 billion from National Housing bank.

items.statement: First-ever co-lending tie-up with large PSU bank and first-ever MSME funding from all-India financial institution in Q4
items.quote: To meet long term business growth, we have done our first-ever co-lending tie-up with a large PSU bank. And also, we had a first ever in the industry funding by MSME sector promoting all-India financial institution.

items.statement: OPEX-to-asset ratio improved 10 bps to 3.58% in FY24 from 3.68% in FY23
items.quote: Our consistent efforts to optimize costs have resulted in improvement of Opex to-asset ratio by 10 bps from 3.68% in FY'23 to 3.58% in FY'24.

items.statement: Digital/eMitra/Mitra channels now ~13% of disbursements vs ~10% earlier, rest hybrid direct/connector
items.quote: If you look at the mix of digital, the eMitra, the Mitra and those channels, we were conventionally at around 10%. As we speak and we close the year, we are around 13%. And these are typically the OPEX-light kind of models which are there. And the rest of that I'd say is a hybrid of the direct channel and some part of the connector channel which is there.

items.statement: MSME book now 17% of AUM, 24% of FY24 disbursements
items.quote: Now that book has become around 17% of total AUM. And last year we did a disbursement, out of that I think 24% is in MSME side.

items.statement: ROA 3.28%, ROE 13.94% for FY24
items.quote: ROA stood at 3.28% and ROE was 13.94% for FY'24.

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio 43.99%, net worth Rs 37,733 million as of March 2024
items.quote: We are well capitalized with the net worth of Rs. 37,733 million and capital adequacy ratio is 43.99%.

items.statement: Employee count 6,075 as of March 2024 vs 6,034 a year ago; net addition ~40
items.quote: The employee count was 6,075 as on March 31, 2024, versus 6,034 as of March 31, 2023.

items.statement: Restructured accounts under RBI Resolution Framework 2.0: Rs 712.3 million outstanding, 80% in 0-30 DPD, classified as Stage-2
items.quote: During Financial Year 2022, a resolution plan was implemented for certain borrower accounts as per RBI's Resolution Framework 2.0 dated 5th of May 2021. Basis the perceived risk and as a matter of prudence, some such accounts with an outstanding amount of Rs. 712.3 million as on 31st of March 2024, have been classified as Stage-2, and provided for as per regulatory guidelines. Out of Rs. 712.3 mil

items.statement: FY25 pre-sales target of Rs 17,500 crore, implying over 20% growth
items.quote: We are guiding to pre-sales growth of a little over 20% with 17,500 crores as a pre-sales target for Fiscal ‘25.

items.statement: FY25 embedded EBITDA margin guided at 31% vs 30% in FY24
items.quote: So, we have guided to 31% embedded EBITDA margin for Fiscal ‘25 compared to 30% for Fiscal ‘24.

items.statement: FY25 operating cash flow guided at Rs 65 billion
items.quote: we generated 57 billion of operating cash for Fiscal ‘24 and are guiding to about 65 billion for Fiscal ’25.

items.statement: FY25 construction spend targeted above Rs 5,000 crore
items.quote: Our construction spend last year at just about 3,600 crores, was lower than what we had planned for and therefore we are in a meaningful manner ramping up the construction spend that we are doing this year and going above 5,000 crores.

items.statement: FY25 new project launches planned with GDV of Rs 12,000 crore
items.quote: During this year, we have planned launches from sites that we have already identified and have GDV about 12,000 crores.

items.statement: FY25 net debt expected near Rs 5,000 crore
items.quote: we suspect it will be close to 5,000 crores of net debt at the end of the fiscal

items.statement: FY25 new business development spend of Rs 3,500-4,000 crore
items.quote: New business development about 35 to 40 billion.

items.statement: FY25 Palava and Upper Thane pre-sales growth of at least 30%
items.quote: we would be looking for at least 30% growth, if not more in this fiscal

items.statement: Annual land sales target of Rs 400-500 crore
items.quote: In terms of land sales, we ar e targeting about $50 million, about 400 crores to 500 crores a year of money from land

items.statement: Housing demand to continue scaling up due to wage growth, mortgages, demographics, urbanization
items.quote: We believe that with steady wage growth, ongoing increase in economic act ivity as well as the plentiful availability of mortgages, combined with India’s demographics and urbanization trends, the demand for housing will only continue to scale up in the years to come

items.statement: FY24 embedded EBITDA margin at 31% despite one-third JDA sales mix
items.quote: The embedded EBITDA margin for our business was at about 31% and this 31% has been achieved this quarter in spite of the fact that we had a higher contribution of sales with almost over one-third of our sales coming from JDA projects

items.statement: Bangalore project margins at 28%, slightly below company average
items.quote: In terms of the margin in Bangalore, we were at about 28% for the sales that we have done so far. So, slightly lower than our overall blend at 30%, 31%

items.statement: FY24 pre-sales of Rs 14,500 crore, up 20% YoY
items.quote: we closed the year with pre-sales of Rs.14,500 crores, which is about 20% growth from last year.

items.statement: FY24 new business development added GDV of Rs 20,000 crore, above guidance of Rs 17,500 crore
items.quote: we added about 20,000 crores of GDV through new projects, which was higher than our guidance of 17,500 crores.

items.statement: FY25 delivery target of 10,000+ units vs ~8,000 units in FY24
items.quote: We delivered just around 8,000 units last year. This year for Fiscal ‘25, we are targeting a five-digit number of 10,000 or more units.

items.statement: FY24 average price growth of 5.5%, supportive of affordability given 9-10% wage growth
items.quote: In terms of pricing, in line with our guidance, we had an overall average price growth of approximately 5.5% for Fiscal ‘24. This we believe is strongly supportive of affordability because wage growth definitely has been closer to the 9-10% mark

items.statement: JDA contribution peaked at one-third of sales; target mix 60% owned land, 40% JDA
items.quote: we had a higher contribution of sales with almost over one-third of our sales coming from JDA projects, which tend to be lower in terms of EBITDA margin. We are now close to the steady state mix that we expect in terms of JDA contribution

items.statement: New GDV additions expected 50% JDA, 50% outright to maintain 60:40 sales mix
items.quote: Therefore for to maintain this 60:40 mix is likely that the incremental GDP addition will be perhaps 50% from JDAs and 50% from owned land.

items.statement: Bangalore sales predominantly to end-users, no speculative bulk buying
items.quote: most of the sales have happened to end users. People are buying for themselves. There’s nobody buying bulk units to trade later.

items.statement: Mumbai market share ~10%; top 5 developers share in mid-20s; consolidation runway long
items.quote: Our market share in Mumbai is at around 10% and the market share of the top five developers in Mumbai is still in the mid-20s. So, there is a long, long way of consolidation to go.

items.statement: Pune market share reached 5% in FY24; target 12-15% by end of decade
items.quote: for the year-ending March ‘24 we have achieved market share in Pune of about 5%, which is a major milestone in our journey to getting to about 15% market share by the end of the decade

items.statement: Government budget scheme for first-time home buyers expected post-election to support affordable housing
items.quote: we hope that the government’s announcement in the budget to bring in a scheme to help first-time home buyers will come in after the election and will help the first-time home buyers and affordable home buyers to get on to the housing ladder.

items.statement: Net debt at Rs 3,000 crore post-QIP (0.2x equity); pre-QIP Rs 6,000 crore (0.4x equity); ceiling 0.5x
items.quote: our net debt now stands at about Rs.3,000 crores, taking into account the impact of this QIP, which is at less than 0.2 times of equity. If we were to exclude the impact of the QIP, our net debt would be at about Rs.6,000 crores, which would also be about 0.4 or less than 0.4x of equity

items.statement: Average cost of funds at 9.4%, down 10 bps in Q4 FY24; further reduction expected post rating upgrade
items.quote: We are now at about 9.4%, which is down about 10 basis points during the quarter and this was prior to the impact of the QIP and the rating upgrade, and therefore, we expect to further work with our lending partners to further improve our cost of funds.

items.statement: QIP raised capital in March 2024; net debt reduced to Rs 3,000 crore (0.2x equity)
items.quote: As you are aware, we have raised a meaningful amount of capital towards the end of the last fiscal in March and that capital will become growth fuel for us both for improvement of the bottom line as well as for strengthening our growth prospects

items.statement: Warehousing JV with Bain and Ivanhoe Cambridge has two assets under development; land acquisition slower than expected
items.quote: we have two assets which are under development currently. One of those assets is actually about to become operational. Cons truction is almost complete. We ar e still in the process of acquiring land. The ramp up has been slower than what we would have liked it to

items.statement: Pune team grew from 80 to 450 people; hiring at one person per day at peak
items.quote: Our Pune team has grown from just 80 to 450 people in few years. We have built local capability across all the functions including customer care, business development, design, construction, etc. At one point in time we were adding one new person a day to team.

items.statement: FY24 implied underlying PAT ~Rs 2,500 crore (~18% of pre-sales); ROE target ~20%
items.quote: Based on the embedded EBITDA of approximately 30% for the full year and 31% for the last quarter, the implied underlying PAT for our business is at about Rs.2,500 crores, about 18% of the pre-sales done during the year, and that puts us in a good position to achieve our ROE objectives of about 20%.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions remain a pervasive risk to sentiment and macro indicators
items.quote: the global situation has been full of various challenges, including geopolitical tensions. This is a risk which is pervasive and in front of our eyes and from time-to-time it is definitely likely to have Macrotech Developers Limited April 25, 2024 impact on the overall sentiment as well as the direction of several macroeconomic indicators

items.statement: Management guides 75% to 100% growth for NPST in coming years, maintaining 15% Q-on-Q growth trend
items.quote: So, this year I can say that we still maintain the 75 odd, 75% to 100% growth rate. That is what we should be looking at.

items.statement: Management aspires to maintain same growth track record for next three years considering India's digital payment growth and global absorption
items.quote: So, Parikshit, if we are looking at three years horizon, for me right now to predict what will happen three years later, I mean, I can still say that we would like to maintain the same track record for the next three years

items.statement: UPI ecosystem monthly transactions at 12-13 billion, anticipated to reach 30 billion and beyond with merchant transition and new products like credit card on UPI
items.quote: the incremental traffic in UPI ecosystem, the tremendous increase which the ecosystem is giving right now which is 12-13 billion is monthly transaction. We anticipate this being taken to 30 billion and much more beyond that.

items.statement: TimePay launched in pilot phase first week of February with 250,000 customers and averaging 100,000 transactions daily
items.quote: We have about 250,000 odd customers on our platform already and we are doing about averaging about 100,000 transactions every day.

items.statement: Evoke platform has approximately 100 aggregators and 14 banks as customers with merchant penetration of about 10,000
items.quote: are approx. 100 aggregators, as of now and about 14 banks you can say. Parikshit Kabra: 14 banks, TSP. Got it. Deepak Thakur: The penetration for the merchants which we are calculating the downline is about 10,000 odd

items.statement: Added four banks in merchant acquiring space for offline payment product Qynx with about 20,000 additional merchants
items.quote: we got four banks, whom we were able to acquire in the merchant acquiring space. We were able to get about 20,000 odd additional merchants on this platform

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded from 30% to 33.5% in FY24; management expects to maintain or slightly improve margins but costs will increase with scale
items.quote: Even if you look at the EBITDA contribution, EBITDA percentage growth, it has gone from 30% to 33.5%.

items.statement: Management will maintain current margins or slightly more, but costs will increase with scale and new business acquisition
items.quote: We will maintain, we will either maintain this margin or it will be slightly more than that.

items.statement: Revenue split shifted to 70% API/Evoke and 30% TSP in FY24; management sees 30-70 ratio going forward but big TSP order wins could shift back to 60-40
items.quote: by the time we ended the year, we are seeing that API would contribute about 70% odd and the TSP would contribute about 30% odd.

items.statement: New products launched: Bharat Bill Payment, Online Dispute Resolution, Qynx offline payments, AutoPay, Payout APIs, Cash on UPI; payer solution in POC stage
items.quote: We added two more products including Bharat Bill payment, which has great scope going forward. We not only added that product last year, but we also got to order book. At the same time, we also added online dispute resolution

items.statement: Cash flow will be deployed for hiring leaders and talent, and potentially acquiring/accelerating product development to shorten time-to-market
items.quote: So, these are two very specific areas where the organization will be empowered now. Thanks to this cash flow. So, that's why our decision will be slower in terms of deployment because we have a lot in our hand.

items.statement: Platform scaled to handle about a billion transactions and managing about 20 million customer base
items.quote: how we are scaling our system to do about a billion transactions. That is what our goal was. How do we reach a billion transactions on our platform? And at the same time doing about, you know, managing about 20 millio n odd customer base on this platform

items.statement: Added senior leadership in marketing, HR, and executive director at board level; brought in FinTech veteran Ram Rastogi to board; focus on building second and third line leadership
items.quote: we were able to add senior leadership in marketing and HR and also we were able to add executive director at board level who has tremendous business acumen around domestic as well the global scale. And not only that, I hope you all are aware, we have also strengthened our board by bringing Mr. Ram Rastogi

items.statement: Added VP-level HR and marketing resources last quarter; structuring team around investor relations and financial analysts; ESOP policy with 2% overall budget, 30-40% utilized
items.quote: We added a very senior VP level resource at HR which wasn’t there ea rlier at all. And now the core KRA for the leader is to bring in the second line and third line in the

items.statement: Revenue grew 216% YoY to 130 crore in FY24; EBITDA grew 252% to 43 crore; net profit grew from 6.5 crore to 26.7 crore; EPS from 3.36 to 13.78
items.quote: 41 crore, which was last financial year, I think we did more than that in the last quarter itself, which made about 130 crore the entire financial year '24. Almost 216% growth.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 revenue 44.7 crore (108% YoY), EBITDA 34.2% margin (15.3% YoY growth), net profit 10 crore (160% YoY)
items.value: Revenue 44.7 crore, EBITDA margin 34.2%, PAT 10 crore
items.quote: our quarterly result, which last year our revenue, which was about 21.4 crore has gone up by about 108%, maybe we have got 44.7 crore in revenue. EBITDA, which was about 6.63 crore has gone up by about 15.3% and the overall percentage, which was about 13.9%, has gone to about 34.2%.

items.statement: Razorpay's switch launch strengthens their position but they are not NPST's customer; NPST sits between banks and payment aggregators, sees opportunity to make customers more competitive
items.quote: Now that opens up opportunity for us, whether we have much stronger performing engine, and can I bring such kind of engine where they can now compete with Razorpay.

items.statement: CBDC is top priority in product roadmap; not part of specific RBI pilot programs but preparing switch for CBDC when other banks enter fray
items.quote: CBDC is part of the top priority in our product roadmap where we are looking forward to getting a breakthrough in this opportunity.

items.statement: Global expansion efforts ongoing but no revenue commitment for FY25; substantial value addition expected in two years; currently absorbed in domestic market
items.quote: This year, although we are making all the efforts, we will still not commit any number coming from the global expansion. We are making all the efforts, but two years down the line, we see that it will substantially add value to the organization

items.statement: Key risks: slowing down pace and losing edge; need to continuously increase alliances and relations; concern about missing investment opportunities
items.quote: Our pace, if we slow down, we see that we may lose the edge. That is one big risk. Second is, we have to ensure that we continue to continue to increase our alliances and relations as much as we can in the industry.

items.statement: Evoke API business is volume-based pay-per-transaction model; pricing varies by financial vs non-financial APIs and value-added services
items.quote: Majorly what we are doing is, we are selling a payment platform-as-a-service. So, the model may change from merchant to merchant and client to client.

items.statement: AI/ML investment focused on fraud prediction, risk reduction, and productizing solutions for merchants; not just for scaling but for value addition and global reach
items.quote: is there a pr ediction about fraud? Is there a possibility to reduce the risk associated with the payment business? So, these are challenges that we have come across during our journey

items.statement: Focus on small finance banks and RRBs for TSP business; large banks have long sales cycles, opportunity mainly in new product launches
items.quote: So, our target is simple. What are the new product requirements across banking domains? And if so, what are the entry criteria when it comes to large banks? And what is the entry criteria for the other segments?

items.statement: Organization has good operating cash flow; cash balance expected to grow significantly with 75-100% growth guidance
items.quote: See, there are two areas that is concerning fo r us and that’s why we need cash. One is, how quickly we are scaling

items.statement: 2:1 bonus issue completed; dividend policy not discussed but investor relations function being strengthened
items.quote: Commitment to shareholders was also done with about 2 is to 1 bonus issue.

items.statement: Technical decline rates less than NPCI requirements; further split between switch and core banking shows even lower numbers
items.quote: We are less than the required decline by NTCI. That is very clear. And at the same time, if we further split between our switch and the core banking, the number will further go down
